title: Two heirs in a year
hook: his son Kharak Singh sickened and died, and his grandson Nau Nihal Singh was killed by a falling arch

segments.voice: Yesterday, his death, and your line, even kings fell short. Today, the kingdom without its founder.

A young prince walks back from his father's cremation, through a gateway in Lahore. He's strong, clever, already a commander, the heir the court was watching. Mourners walk with him, the smoke of the pyre still in their clothes. Overhead, stones shift. The archway comes down, and the prince is struck. The kingdom that looked so solid has cremated one king that morning, and now its heir is down among the fallen stones.
screen: `BACK FROM A FATHER'S CREMATION.` → `A GATEWAY IN LAHORE.` → `THE ARCH COMES DOWN.`

segments.voice: Kharak Singh, the Maharaja's eldest son, took the throne. Histories describe him as gentle and not suited to the hard politics of the court. Power slipped quickly into other hands, among them his own son's and the ministers'. His favorite adviser was killed, and later Kharak Singh himself fell ill and died. Some at the time suspected poison; nobody can say for certain. His son, Nau Nihal Singh, was young, able and ambitious, already ruling in all but name. On the day of his father's cremation, as he passed under a gateway, part of it fell and struck him, and he died of his injuries. Histories record the suspicion that it was no accident. Some point to the ministers who gained from his death, and say the story of the hours after was kept close. Others say the arch simply fell. The sources don't settle it, and i won't pretend they do. The Maharaja had spent a lifetime building a kingdom. Within a short time of his death, his son and grandson were both gone, and the throne was open to whoever could seize it. A kingdom can look like a fortress and still hang by a thread, or by the stones of one gateway.
screen: `KHARAK SINGH TAKES THE THRONE AND FALLS ILL.` · `NAU NIHAL SINGH AND THE FALLING ARCH.` · `AN ACCIDENT, OR NOT?` · `A KINGDOM HANGING BY A THREAD.` · then, large: `POWER IS FRAGILE.`

segments.voice: Think of one kind of power you hold, a role in your family, money, health, influence over someone, and picture honestly, without fear, how it could be gone tomorrow. Then ask what would still be there if it went, and rest in that, breath by breath. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.
Kharak Singh, who sickened and died; his son Nau Nihal Singh was struck by a falling arch on the day of his father's cremation, two heirs lost in a year.
Your line: power is fragile. A throne is only as steady as the people around it. Day nine hundred twenty-six, done.
